types.doc:
A fixed-ceiling ring of elements. The storage is a plain array with the
 live elements starting at `head` and wrapping around, so every operation
 that touches an end is constant time whatever the length.

 `capacity` is a ceiling, not a reservation: the array starts empty and is
 doubled — up to the ceiling — as the buffer fills, and empty slots beyond
 `len` hold copies of an element already in the buffer. Those stale copies
 are outside every view the buffer hands out.

types.doc:
A d-ary heap: a heap laid out in a contiguous array where every node has up
 to `arity` children.

 A binary heap does one comparison per level; a 4-ary heap does three but
 halves the number of levels, and the children of one node sit next to each
 other in memory, so a wider heap usually wins on modern caches. `arity: 4` is
 Boost.Heap's default for `d_ary_heap`.

 The heap is a multiset: it does not remove duplicates, and its iteration
 order is the internal array order, which is only partially ordered. Use
 `into_sorted_array` when the order matters.

 ```mbt check
 test {
   let heap : @heap.DaryHeap[Int32] = try! @heap.DaryHeap::new()
   heap.push(3)
   heap.push(1)
   heap.push(2)
   assert_true(heap.peek() == Some(1))
   assert_true(heap.pop() == Some(1))
   assert_true(heap.length() == 2)
 }
 ```

A monotone heap over `UInt64` keys: the key of a pushed entry may not be
 smaller than the key of the last one popped. Under that rule a pop costs
 O(log C) where C is the width of the key space, and it never compares two

 reordered.

 ```mbt check
   heap.push(1UL, "one")
   heap.push(9UL, "nine")
   assert_true(heap.pop_min() == Some((1UL, "one")))
   assert_true(heap.pop_min() == Some((5UL, "five")))
 }
 ```

A Fenwick tree: `tree[i]` holds the sum of the `i & -i` elements that end at

 ```mbt check
   assert_true(fenwick.range_sum(1, 3) == 4)
   let _ = fenwick.set(0, 10)
   assert_true(fenwick.get(0) == Some(10))
   assert_true(fenwick.lower_bound(5) == Some(0))
 }
 ```

 two buckets, and the second bucket is computed from the fingerprint alone,
 so a removal does not have to remember where the item went. An insert that
 cannot place its fingerprint after a bounded number of kicks reports failure
 instead of looping, which is the one thing a Cuckoo filter trades away: its
 false-positive rate, unlike a Bloom filter's, stays flat as it fills.

 ```mbt check

   let filter : @sketch.CuckooFilter[String] = @sketch.CuckooFilter::new(
     expected_items=100,
   )
   assert_true(filter.insert("a"))
   assert_true(filter.may_contain("a"))
   assert_true(filter.remove("a"))
   assert_true(!filter.may_contain("a"))
 }
 ```

types.doc:
Many patterns matched in one pass: a trie whose nodes also carry failure
 links, so the text is read once and every occurrence is reported as soon as
 its last code unit is read. Overlapping matches all appear, including
 suffixes of longer ones, which the output chain walks without visiting nodes
 that match nothing. Build is O(total pattern length), search O(n + matches).

 those that end at the same place. A zero-length pattern is reported at every
 offset, before the matches ending at that offset.

 ```mbt check

   let ac = @text.AhoCorasick::new(["he", "she", "his", "hers"])
   @test.assert_eq(ac.search_all("ushers").to_array(), [(1, 1), (0, 2), (3, 2)])
   assert_true(ac.is_match("ushers"))
   assert_false(ac.is_match("us"))
 }
 ```

 lets a generated module carry one as a literal; `from_layout` re-derives
 every slot from the keys and refuses a layout that does not fit them.

 ```mbt check
 test {
   let builder : @phf.PhfBuilder[String, Int32] = @phf.PhfBuilder::new()
   builder.entry("a", 1)
   builder.entry("b", 2)
   let table = builder.build()
   assert_true(table.get("a") == Some(1))
   assert_true(table.get("b") == Some(2))
   assert_true(table.get("c") == None)
   assert_true(table.length() == 2)
 }
 ```

The first difference of adjacent elements: element 0 is kept, element `i`

free_fns.name: all_equal
free_fns.doc:
Whether every element of the run is equal to every other. Empty and
 single-element runs are equal by vacuity.

free_fns.name: all_unique
free_fns.doc: Whether all elements are distinct, using a hash set of the values seen.

free_fns.name: apply_permutation_in_place
free_fns.doc:
Rearranges the run so that the element that was at position `i` moves to
 position `order[i]`.

 `order` must be a permutation of `0..a.length()`. When it is not, or when
 its length differs from the run's, the run is left unchanged. The
 rearrangement uses cycle following, so it needs no second copy of the run.

free_fns.name: at_most_one
free_fns.doc: Whether at most one element satisfies `pred`. Stops at the second match.

free_fns.name: bisect_left
free_fns.doc:
The first index at which `value` could be inserted while keeping `a`
 ascending: every element before the result is smaller than `value`.

 `a` must already be sorted ascending. The result is in `0..=a.length()`.

 trait cannot express.

free_fns.name: bisect_right
free_fns.doc:
The first index past every element equal to `value`: every element before
 the result is less than or equal to `value`.

 `a` must already be sorted ascending. The result is in `0..=a.length()`.

free_fns.name: bisect_right_by
free_fns.sig: fn<T> bisect_right_by(ArrayView[T], T, cmp~ : (T, T) -> Int32) -> Int32
free_fns.doc:

 trait cannot express.

free_fns.doc: Splits a sequence into runs in which each adjacent pair satisfies `same`.

free_fns.name: chunks

free_fns.name: partial_sort_in_place
free_fns.doc:
Partially orders the run so that the first `k` elements are the `k`
 smallest, in ascending order. The rest stays in the run in no particular
 order. `k` is clamped to the run length.

free_fns.doc:
Splits the run into the elements satisfying `pred` and the rest, both in

free_fns.name: partition_in_place
free_fns.doc:
Groups the run so that every element satisfying `pred` comes first, and
 returns the boundary: the number of elements that satisfy `pred`.
 Unstable and linear.

free_fns.doc:
Applies `f` to every element: the mapped results keep their original order
 in the first array, the elements for which `f` returns `None` keep theirs

free_fns.doc:
The first index for which `pred` is false, assuming every true element
 precedes every false one. The result is in `0..=a.length()`.

Running combination without an identity element: element `i` of the result

free_fns.doc:
Rearranges the run into the previous lexicographic permutation, returning

free_fns.name: reservoir_sample
free_fns.sig: fn<T> reservoir_sample(Iter[T], k~ : Int32, seed? : UInt64) -> Array[T]
free_fns.doc:
Draws `k` elements from the sequence, each element ending up in the result
 with probability `k / n` — reservoir sampling, so the length of the
 sequence need not be known in advance and the sequence is read once.

 The result keeps the drawn elements in the order they were read: the first
 `k` fill the reservoir as they arrive, and a later element replaces one of
 them at a position drawn uniformly. `k` at or above the length returns every
 element in order; a `k` of zero or less returns nothing.

 The draw is a function of the stream and `seed`, and of nothing else, so the
 same seed gives the same sample. Pass one whenever a run has to be
 reproducible; without it the process-wide seed is used, which differs
 between runs.

 ```mbt check
 test {
   let run : Array[Int32] = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
   let all = @algo.reservoir_sample(run.iter(), k=9, seed=1UL)
   assert_eq(all, [10, 20, 30, 40, 50])
   let one = @algo.reservoir_sample(run.iter(), k=2, seed=1UL)
   assert_eq(one.length(), 2)
   assert_eq(one, @algo.reservoir_sample(run.iter(), k=2, seed=1UL))
 }
 ```

 does not change. `n` is clamped to the run.

 C++20's `std::shift_right` leaves the head in an unspecified state; this
 function makes the state deterministic by duplicating the boundary element.

free_fns.doc:
Yields elements while `pred` holds, and also yields the first element for

free_fns.doc:
Splits a sequence into two independent iterators over the same elements.

free_fns.doc: The distinct elements of the run in order of first appearance.

free_fns.doc:
Every contiguous window of `size` elements, left to right: `n - size + 1`

 ```mbt check
 }
 ```

free_fns.sig: fn<A, B> zip_longest(Iter[A], Iter[B], fill~ : A, fill_b~ : B) -> Iter[(A, B)]
free_fns.doc:
Pairs elements while both sequences have them, then pairs the leftovers of
 the longer one with the corresponding fill value.
